content_md:
Making a prediction post to help test [@Mike Casey](https://caseyjr.org/blyg/) prediction thingie.
```
{ 
"claim": "The Riemann hypothesis proof by AI will check out while the human proof that was rushed out today will prove to have a flaw",
"probability": 0.8,
"resolves_by": "2027-06-30",
"criteria": "Consensus of mathematics community" }
```
Comments: Hmm... I'm a bit uncomfortable being locked into a particular structure of the claim. Could we generalize it so many more claim structures are possible? In particular, I think probability is a meaningless measure in cases like this. Here, I'd rather just rank the 4 possible ways this could go (both are right, one is right/other is wrong, both are wrong). I also think Knightian uncertainty needs to be somehow be in the awareness here. Like what if an asteroid destroys the earth before the resolution. Did the claim resolve or not?
